title: Distributed Web Intelligence Crawling & Change Detection Platform with Playwright, Celery & Redis Bloom Filters
problem: Manual competitive market monitoring is error-prone, unscalable, and blind to dynamic client-side DOM mutations. Naive HTTP scrapers fail completely on modern Single Page Applications (SPAs) that require JavaScript execution, trigger immediate IP bans due to uncoordinated request rates, and repeatedly re-crawl identical URLs wasting network bandwidth. This project builds a distributed web intelligence crawling and change detection platform in Python. The system coordinates headless browser scraping using Playwright and Celery worker queues, prevents duplicate URL crawls using Redis Bloom filters, stores structured page entity snapshots in PostgreSQL, computes content and structural DOM diffs, and sends automated webhook alerts upon detecting significant changes.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Competitor Price & Stock Monitoring
use_cases.first_sentence: Retail pricing intelligence teams need to monitor thousands of competitor product listings daily to adjust promotional pricing dynamically.
use_cases.second_sentence: The crawler executes headless browser sessions, extracts live pricing and stock availability from dynamic JavaScript storefronts, and flags price changes in PostgreSQL.

use_cases.title: Technology Job Market Skill Trend Intelligence
use_cases.first_sentence: Workforce planning analysts require structured insights into evolving technical requirements across corporate career portals and job boards.
use_cases.second_sentence: The platform schedules periodic crawls of designated employer domains, parses required engineering competencies, and aggregates monthly technology demand trends.

use_cases.title: Corporate Regulatory Disclosure & Policy Tracking
use_cases.first_sentence: Compliance auditing teams must track updates across governmental regulatory portal announcements and corporate privacy policy terms.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine computes structural semantic diffs across crawled policy page snapshots, dispatching immediate notification summaries when legal clauses are revised.

hard_parts: Orchestrating headless Playwright browser contexts in Celery worker processes with strict memory recycling to prevent browser zombie leaks
Implementing scalable URL deduplication using space-efficient Redis Bloom filters across millions of discovered web hyperlinks
Designing semantic DOM diffing algorithms that ignore dynamic ad trackers and timestamps while accurately detecting substantive text/price changes
Enforcing per-domain rate limiting and polite crawl delays with exponential backoff to avoid IP blocks
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating crawler task queues, Playwright browser managers, Bloom filter utilities, and diff engines
Automated load benchmark report verifying 120+ pages per minute extraction throughput across headless JavaScript workers
Anti-fake verification script dynamically modifying a target mock SPA product price and verifying the platform detects the delta and emits a change event

components.name: Redis Bloom Filter URL Deduplicator

components.purpose: Spawns isolated Chromium contexts, waits for selector hydration, and extracts structured DOM elements

architecture.data_flow: Users register target URLs via the FastAPI endpoint; the scheduler checks the Redis Bloom filter; if the URL has not been crawled in the current cycle, a task dispatches to the Celery queue; a Celery worker launches a Playwright Chromium context, navigates to the target page, waits for network idle, and extracts structured JSON attributes; the worker writes the raw snapshot to PostgreSQL; the diff engine computes a SHA-256 hash and compares with the previous crawl; if changes are detected, a semantic diff generates and triggers a notification webhook.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Redis Bloom filter capacity checks preventing duplicate crawl dispatches; Playwright navigation timeout limits (max 15s) killing hung browser contexts.

targets.target: Deduplication accuracy is >= 99.8% with false positive suppression < 0.2%

targets.target: Average notification dispatch latency is < 3.2 seconds across 20 trials
targets.report: Change detection timing summary table and webhook audit report

Understanding of browser automation (Playwright/Puppeteer), DOM manipulation, and HTTP scraping ethics

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU and network I/O bound web scraping and data processing)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local mock SPA and Docker containers)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or proxy subscriptions required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop (Redis, PostgreSQL containers), Python 3.11, and Playwright Chromium
environment.fallback_path: Local static HTML file scraping with BeautifulSoup if Playwright browser dependencies fail to install

riskiest_component.name: Browser Process Zombie Leaks and Memory Exhaustion in Celery Workers
riskiest_component.mitigation: Configure Celery worker_max_tasks_per_child (e.g. 50 tasks) to recycle worker processes and close browser contexts explicitly in finally blocks.
riskiest_component.fallback: Run browser contexts inside lightweight ephemeral Docker containers.
